title: Sharing files safely: who can open your link

audience.who: Corporate employees who share documents from cloud storage in their daily work
audience.knows: How to click Share and paste a link into an email or chat; not what each link setting actually allows
audience.cares_about: Getting a colleague the file quickly without it reaching people who should not see it, and not creating a problem they have to explain later

outcome: Before sharing a document, the viewer can pick the narrowest link setting that still works, choose view or edit on purpose, and know when to switch the link off.
through_line: A link is a key that travels: whoever holds it can use it, so choose who the key opens for before you send it, and take it back when the job is done.

must_cover.what: What each link setting lets people do: anyone with the link, people in the company, named people
View versus edit: what each permission lets a holder do
How a link forwarded once can reach people the sender never meant
The few checks to make before sharing a document
What to do when access is no longer needed

must_avoid: Naming or showing any real cloud storage product or its exact menu wording; settings are described generically, since names differ between tools
Fear, blame or scare statistics; any figure or breach story without a source on the approved knowledge sheet
Legal, compliance or company-policy claims; the lesson says to follow the company's own rules and does not state them
Opening with a dictionary-style explanation or an agenda; a lecture voice
Claims that a setting is technically unbreakable: forwarding is about the link, not hacking
example_posture: One running example: a colleague sharing an ordinary work document (a project plan or budget draft) with a few teammates, then the same link forwarded onward. Plausible and low drama, a calm everyday workplace, one person at a time.
visual_direction: One hand-drawn marker world on a white board, drawn as it is spoken. A document and a link shown as a key that travels; people as simple drawn figures only as the narration needs them; the three settings as three rings of who can reach it, widening and narrowing; view versus edit as what a holder can do to the page; a forward as a line passing the link onward; a short checklist ticked on the board. Mostly drawn pictures that change; few text-only boards; one accent mark for the point at a time.
voice_note: A calm, capable colleague who has seen this go wrong once and says so lightly; practical, never alarmed, never talking down. Short sentences, concrete nouns.
open_questions: No source document was supplied: all must_cover points are from the requester's notes, so the fact-finder must ground them in general, tool-neutral best practice on the knowledge sheet.
Company-specific link defaults and policy are unknown; the script should point viewers to their own organisation's rules rather than state any.
